At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **recent-intent residual SASRec with multi-negative training**. Improvements remain hypotheses; no validation results are available.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already learns selective history dependence; a recent branch needs controls demonstrating benefits beyond added capacity. Repeated recent interests motivate testing it, not assuming its superiority. (2) Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. These motivate discrimination experiments but do not establish validation HR@10. (3) Similar embedding alignment across categories provides little justification for prioritizing collapse penalties. Empty category breakdowns cannot identify category-specific causes.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates calibrated multi-negative training, but its theorem depends on the sampling distribution. Excluding every known positive changes that distribution. (2) [R²NS](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) supports uniform warm-up before harder sampling; false negatives discourage immediate hardest-negative mining. (3) [LSIDN](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.14743) motivates separating persistent and current interests without establishing purchase satisfaction. (4) [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) motivates a zero-initialized residual: adding output LayerNorm would change baseline scores even with a zero residual.

**Framework and candidate directions.** Separate temporal evidence, discrimination, and relation evidence.
